user_message: Put credit spread on IWM, expiry in a fortnight. Short leg 30 delta, long leg 5 points lower. I open it on Friday 15:30 ET but only if IWM closed lower the day before. Out at 50% of max profit, or when the loss is two times the credit I received, or at expiry, whatever comes first. Account 50k, I risk 2% of account on each trade and gains are reinvested.

author.intent: Backtest on IWM options from 2024-01-18 to the latest data: on Fridays at 15:30 New York time, only if IWM's close on the previous trading day (Thursday) was below the close of the day before that, sell a put credit spread expiring about 14 days later, with the short put nearest 30 delta and the long put 5 dollars lower in strike. Exit at the first of: profit equal to 50% of the credit received (spread price down 50%); loss equal to twice the credit received (spread price up 200%, i.e. three times the credit); or expiration. Starting account 50,000 dollars; each trade is sized so that its maximum loss is 2% of the current account value, with gains reinvested.
author.if_asked: Fortnight is 14 days, so the expiry two Fridays later. Closed lower the day before means Thursday close under Wednesday close. Risk is the max loss of the spread, width minus credit, and it should be 2% of what the account is worth at that moment. Period is all the option data you have.
author.also_fine: Sizing the 2% risk on the stop-loss amount (twice the credit) instead of the spread's maximum loss is acceptable if stated.
